<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR adds C++ group-aware CPU shared-memory kernels for all-gather, all-to-all, and all-reduce, enabling communication within arbitrary process groups instead of assuming the communication group is the global world, which is required to support combined SP and TP on CPU.

## Modifications

1.  Add new CPU SHM kernels: shm_group_allgather, shm_group_allreduce, and shm_group_alltoall, with group-aware all-to-all added to support Ulysses SP communication on CPU.
2. Add per-ProcessGroup SHM contexts with independent workspaces, buffers, rank information, and synchronization states. Previously, SHM collectives assumed that the communication group was the global world. To support multiple parallel groups such as TP and SP, SHM collectives need to operate on the actual ProcessGroup, since the same process may communicate with different peers depending on the collective.
3.  Add unit tests.

> [blocking] group_coordinator.py:209-226: SHM initialization is attempted for CPU groups without checking that every peer is on the same host. shm_initialize waits indefinitely for remote peers' local POSIX SHM objects; gate this path on locality and fall back for cross-node groups.
> 
> [blocking] usp.py:109-114: The CPU path calls shm_alltoall regardless of input size, while the kernel rejects inputs above 32 MiB; it also compares a possible None handle with zero. Please guard both conditions and use the distributed fallback.

Thanks!  I've added the necessary guards and fallback handling to address both issues.
